problem: The caption says 'the same cut shows why longitudinal stress is half the hoop stress'. The diametral cut (cut along a diameter) balances pressure p d L against two wall strips and gives hoop stress only. Longitudinal stress needs a different cut, taken across the axis through the end cap. The flowchart also draws both stresses out of the same 'Balance forces' box, so a student is taught a wrong derivation step.
fix: Caption: 'Cutting the shell along a diameter turns pressure into a force p d L, balanced by two wall forces, giving hoop stress; a second cut across the axis balances the end-cap force p πd²/4 against the wall ring πdt, giving longitudinal stress, half the hoop value.' In the flowchart, keep the diametral-cut chain ending at hoop stress, and add a separate branch from 'Internal pressure p' → 'Cut across axis (end cap)' → 'Balance forces: σ_L π d t = p π d²/4' → 'Longitudinal stress σ_L = p d / 4t'.

problem: 'p d/(2t) uses diameter; p r/t gives the same number, so the slip hides' is muddled. Using p r/t correctly gives the same answer, but dropping the radius value into the d slot halves the result; the sentence does not say which mistake it means.
fix: 'Substituting the radius value into the diameter formula. σ_h = p d/(2t) needs the diameter; σ_h = p r/t with r = d/2 gives the same number, so using r where d is written halves your answer and is easy to miss. Write the formula and the value with the same symbol.'
